name: Progress with steps
summary: Progress for a long task: a bar with a percentage, the time left, each step done, now and next, and a way to keep working while it runs.
use: for long tasks (imports, exports, uploads, migrations) that take more than a few seconds
a11y: The bar is a progressbar with a value and a text value; steps are an ordered list with the current one marked aria-current; a polite status line names the current step; update it when the step changes, not on every percent.
notes: Switch from inline-spinner to this once a task is expected to pass the system's --ds-state-wait-progress-after (10 seconds where the system has it).

use_when: a task takes longer than about 10 seconds
the task has steps the person would recognise
avoid_when: waits of a few seconds: use inline-spinner
unknown length with no steps: say what is happening and show an indeterminate bar

parts.name: title
parts.what: the heading: what happened, in plain words, as in “Importing 4,812 contacts”

parts.name: progress
parts.what: how far the task has got, 0 to 1

parts.name: left
parts.what: time left and what the person can do meanwhile, as in “About 2 minutes left. You can close this page; w”

parts.name: steps.label
parts.what: the visible label, as in “Upload file”

empty.how: Not applicable: this state screen shows no list of records.

loading.how: This part is the long-wait state: a bar, a percentage and the steps.

error.how: A failed step should turn its dot to the danger colour, say what failed and offer Retry from that step; not drawn here.

disabled.how: No control here is ever disabled; each one always does something.

long_text.how: Titles balance and body text wraps at word boundaries inside a capped measure.

keyboard: Tab reaches Cancel import, then Keep working
